outcomes.text: Understand short recordings about everyday needs, including simple shopping transactions, directions and instructions.
Find main points, specific information and details in recordings about everyday subjects.
Understand factual information and ideas from announcements, phone messages, news items, interviews and dialogues on familiar topics.
Understand simple descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, hopes and ambitions.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, emotions and attitudes in predictable spoken texts.
Work out the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Understand short, simple texts such as public signs, notices, restaurant information and transport information.
Find main points, specific information and details in predictable texts such as advertisements, menus and timetables.
Understand authentic texts about familiar topics, including articles, emails, blogs and letters.
Understand simple written descriptions of events, opinions, emotions, hopes and ambitions.
Recognise main points, themes, opinions, ideas, emotions and attitudes in predictable written texts.
Work out the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Take part in short social exchanges and communicate basic needs in familiar situations.
Hold unprepared conversations about familiar personal-interest and everyday topics.
Describe past events and experiences, hopes and ambitions, and briefly explain opinions and plans.
Communicate reasonably accurately using varied structures, tenses and situation-appropriate vocabulary.
Connect short points into a sequence using simple linking words.
Use suitable strategies to keep an interaction going.
Use pronunciation and intonation features to express meaning and attitude.
Complete forms with simple personal details.
Write simple factual information using everyday vocabulary and expressions.
Write linked phrases and sentences about personal life, immediate surroundings and everyday subjects.
Write simple connected texts about familiar topics such as arrangements, preferences, family, education, work and travel.
Describe past events and experiences, opinions, hopes and ambitions, giving brief reasons.
Communicate reasonably accurately using varied structures, time frames and situation-appropriate vocabulary.
Link short written elements into a connected sequence using simple connectors.
Use and understand time expressions, including times, days, weekdays, months and seasons.
Use German vocabulary for dates, times, days, months, seasons, frequency, sequence and time relationships.
Use vocabulary for meals, fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, seafood, snacks, drinks, cutlery and utensils.
Name meals and courses, including breakfast, lunch, dinner, starters, main courses, desserts and snacks.
Identify common fruit and vegetables, and describe vegetarian or vegan food.
Identify common meat, fish and seafood products.
Name common snacks and fast foods, including sweets, crisps, ice cream, pizza and chips.
Name common drinks, including soft drinks, coffee, milk, water, juice and tea.
Identify everyday foods such as bread, butter, eggs, dairy products, pasta, rice, soup, salt, sugar and oil.
Name common kitchen and tableware items, including cutlery, pans, glasses, cups, bowls and plates.
Describe food as fresh, cooked, raw, salty, spicy, sweet or seasoned.
Talk about hunger, thirst, diets, eating, preparing meals, cooking, grilling, cutting, drinking and being full.
Use vocabulary for body parts, health and illness.
Identify major body parts, including limbs, face, organs, joints, skin, hair, mouth, nose, ears, teeth and voice.
Talk about breathing, touching, wearing glasses or hearing aids, baldness, smelling and seeing.
Name health professionals, medical items, medicines and common healthcare locations.
Describe illnesses, symptoms, injuries, treatment, exercise, fitness, health, tiredness and pain.
Use language related to travel and transport.
Name journeys, destinations, travel documents, vehicles, stations, tickets, passengers, luggage, directions and travel problems.
Discuss travelling, walking, cycling, driving, flying, boarding, leaving, parking, crossing roads and getting lost.
Use language to describe oneself, family members and friends.
Use greetings, farewells, thanks, apologies, welcomes, invitations, refusals and expressions of wellbeing.
Express reactions such as interest, annoyance, regret, appreciation and admiration.
Invite people, accept or decline invitations, suggest alternative dates and ask whether someone wants to go out.
Discuss family members, ages, relationships, marriage, children, relatives, siblings, partners and marital status.
Describe people’s age, build, height, hair colour, hair texture and physical appearance.
Describe personality, emotions, moods and qualities such as kindness, intelligence, laziness, happiness and seriousness.
Talk about names, birth, upbringing, relationships, emotions, marriage, living arrangements, ageing and death.
Use vocabulary for rooms, furniture, furnishings, gardens and household appliances.
Name rooms, household spaces, furniture, doors, windows, floors, walls, stairs, balconies and garages.
Identify bathroom items such as towels, toiletries, mirrors, toilets, sinks, showers, taps and toothbrushes.
Describe bathing, showering, washing the face, brushing hair and cleaning teeth.
Name common living-room furniture and objects, including pictures, shelves, sofas, chairs, rugs and tables.
Identify kitchen rooms, containers, appliances and fixtures such as tins, bottles, cupboards, sinks and cookers.
Talk about preparing, reheating, frying, freezing, cooking, grilling, chopping, sewing and eating food.
Name bedroom furniture and furnishings, including beds, bedding, wardrobes, pillows, blankets, lamps and clocks.
Describe getting up, waking, resting, lying down, sleeping, feeling tired and waking someone.
Discuss household chores such as baking, ironing, cleaning, taking out rubbish, clearing and setting the table, vacuuming and washing clothes.
Name garden features including trees, flowers, plants, lawns, walls, fences and front gardens.
Talk about gardening, growing vegetables and planting.
Name household appliances, electronic equipment, energy sources, chargers, plugs, sockets and telephones.
Describe switching devices on or off, opening, closing, moving, breaking and using telephones.
Use German colour vocabulary, including light, dark, blue, brown, yellow, green, orange, purple, pink, red, black, silver and white.
Use language for clothing and accessories.
Name clothing and accessories such as swimwear, shirts, trousers, coats, dresses, shoes, jewellery, bags, watches and glasses.
Discuss clothing size, fit, comfort, style, trying clothes on, dressing, undressing and changing clothes.
Use vocabulary for leisure activities, hobbies and sport.
Talk about fishing, watching films or television, concerts, festivals, music, theatre and listening through headphones.
Discuss playing musical instruments, climbing, painting, singing and drawing.
Name sports, sports equipment, venues, teams, competitions, scores, medals, prizes and sporting activities.
Talk about writing poems or short stories, taking photographs, playing, winning or losing competitions and scoring goals.
Use language for continents, countries, nationalities and compass directions.
Give and understand the four compass directions.
Name the continents and polar regions, including Africa, the Americas, Antarctica, the Arctic, Asia, Europe and Oceania.
Discuss a candidate’s nationality, home country and language.
Use language concerning the natural world, environment, climate and weather.
Name natural features and environmental topics including forests, mountains, rivers, coastlines, weather, climate change, recycling and farming.

Use vocabulary for the digital world, documents and texts.
Know vocabulary for apps, screens, blogs, chats, computers and digital files.
Know vocabulary for printers, films, photographs, mobile phones and information.
Know vocabulary for the internet, maps, laptops, lists and computer mice.
Know vocabulary for USB sticks, messages, online activity, online safety and folders.
Know vocabulary for passwords, PCs, selfies, text messages and software.
Know vocabulary for social networks, games, tablets, keyboards, telephones and touchscreens.
Know vocabulary for websites and advertising.
Use German expressions for calling, accessing the internet, charging and completing forms.
Use German expressions for chatting, downloading, emailing and sending something by email.
Use German verbs for finding, downloading, clicking, copying and posting online.
Use German verbs for sending, saving and surfing.
Know German vocabulary for articles, letters, brochures, books and comics.
Know German vocabulary for forms, magazines, notes, notebooks and postcards.
Know German vocabulary for bills, guidebooks, passports, tickets and periodicals.
Know German vocabulary for newspapers and certificates.
Use language for buildings, services, urban areas and shopping.
Know German vocabulary for lifts, exits, stations, farms, libraries and bookshops.
Know German vocabulary for castles, offices, bus stations, cafés, entrances and admission.
Know German vocabulary for ground floors, factories, fortresses, gyms and outdoor pools.
Know German vocabulary for buildings, houses, hotels, cinemas, clinics and hospitals.
Know German vocabulary for lifts, museums, post offices, restaurants and castles.
Know German vocabulary for schools, swimming pools, stadiums, petrol stations, theatres and zoos.
Know German vocabulary for universities, flats and housing floors.
Know German vocabulary for traffic lights, motorways, bridges, bus stops, villages and corners.
Know German vocabulary for airports, pedestrian crossings, areas, roundabouts and market squares.
Know German vocabulary for neighbourhoods, places, car parks, parking spaces and squares.
Know German vocabulary for playgrounds, towns, districts, streets, underground trains, traffic and crossings.
Know German vocabulary for bakeries, banks, cheap prices, bookshops, stalls and butchers.
Know German vocabulary for banknotes, opening status, shops, sizes and special offers.
Know German vocabulary for waiters, kiosks, loose change, credit cards and customers.
Know German vocabulary for shops, markets, coins, prices, receipts and sales.
Know German vocabulary for supermarkets, expensive goods and items for sale.
Use German expressions for renting a bicycle, shopping, spending money and receiving a refund.
Use German verbs for buying, complaining, selling and asking the price.
Use the German verb for paying.

outcomes.text: Use language related to shopping.
Use vocabulary for materials.
Know German words for cotton, glass, gold, wood and leather.
Know German words for metal, paper, plastic, silver, stone and wool.
Use language for measurements, including size and shape.
Know German vocabulary for degrees, grams, size, kilograms, kilometres, litres, metres and centimetres.
Describe objects as enormous, large, small, short, long, medium-sized, gigantic or tiny.
Know German vocabulary for triangles, circles and squares.
Describe shapes as triangular, round or square.
Use vocabulary for educational institutions, training, classrooms, learning tools, subjects and studying.
Know German vocabulary for departments, vocational schools, directors, education and subjects.
Know German words for primary schools, grammar schools, secondary schools and canteens.
Know German vocabulary for kindergartens, courses, teachers, private schools and pupils.
Know German vocabulary for school terms, schoolyards, school years, universities and preschools.
Know German classroom vocabulary for paper, books, pencil cases, bells, exercise books and interactive boards.
Know German words for glue, pens, rulers, erasers, blackboards, tables and whiteboards.
Know the German word for dictionary.
Know German names for biology, chemistry, geography, foreign languages, history and computing.
Know German names for art, mathematics, music, compulsory subjects, physics and religion.
Know German names for sport, drama, optional subjects and sciences.
Know German vocabulary for tasks, examples, questions, homework, classes and coursework.
Know German vocabulary for classmates, marks, breaks, projects, examinations and results.
Know German vocabulary for school reports, lessons, timetables and exercises.
Use German verbs for answering, passing, failing, explaining and experimenting.
Use German verbs for asking questions, reading, taking notes, writing and studying.
Use German verbs for practising, repeating, understanding and knowing.
Use language for jobs, careers and workplaces.
Know German vocabulary for lawyers, architects, doctors, bakers, farmers, postmen and bus drivers.
Know German vocabulary for interpreters, firefighters, butchers, flight attendants and hairdressers.
Know German vocabulary for engineers, waiters, plumbers, nurses, teachers and bricklayers.
Know German vocabulary for mechanics, police officers, pilots, secretaries and soldiers.
Know German vocabulary for taxi drivers, vets, carpenters and translators.
Know German vocabulary for employees, work, employers, offices, shops and companies.
Know German vocabulary for jobs, earnings and workshops.
Describe being unemployed or promoted and finding, seeking, getting or losing a job.
Use German expressions for being fired, retiring, going on holiday and earning money.
Use German expressions for taking leave.
Use language concerning countries, nationalities, languages, culture, customs, faiths and celebrations.
Know German vocabulary for Hanukkah, Diwali, public holidays, fireworks and wedding celebrations.
Know German vocabulary for wedding anniversaries, churches, mosques, New Year and Easter.
Know German vocabulary for pilgrimages, Ramadan, religion, synagogues, temples and Christmas.
Express believing in God, celebrating and being religious in German.
